intro: Precedence and associativity determine expression grouping. They do not generally determine the temporal order in which operands execute.
outcomes: Rewrite ambiguous expressions for reliable reasoning.
prerequisites: Operators act on operands. Parentheses explicitly group expressions. Side effects include assignments and increments; their execution order must satisfy sequencing rules.

sections.title: 1. Precedence from stronger to weaker
paragraphs: A useful C11 grouping ladder is: postfix calls/subscripts/member access/postfix updates; unary operators and casts; multiplication/division/remainder; addition/subtraction; shifts; relational comparisons; equality; bitwise AND; bitwise XOR; bitwise OR; logical AND; logical OR; conditional ?:; assignment; comma.
Operators in stronger groups bind more tightly. Thus 2 + 3 * 4 groups as 2 + (3 * 4), yielding 14. Parentheses can replace that default: (2 + 3) * 4 yields 20.

Bitwise AND has lower precedence than equality. flags & mask == 0 groups as flags & (mask == 0), which usually is not the desired bit test. Write (flags & mask) == 0. Remembering this failure pattern is more useful than merely reciting a list.

sections.title: 2. Associativity at the same precedence
paragraphs: Most binary arithmetic operators group left to right: 20 / 5 * 2 means (20 / 5) * 2 and yields 8. Assignment groups right to left: a = b = 4 means a = (b = 4). Both objects receive 4, subject to their types.

Unary operations, assignment, and the conditional operator have rightward grouping rules. The middle expression of ?: is treated as if parenthesised. Do not use a compact chain of conditional operators when explicit if/else branches communicate the decision more clearly.

Associativity describes the parse tree, not an instruction schedule. In f() + g(), + groups the operands but does not promise that f executes first. Function argument order is likewise not generally fixed in C11.
example: The first line yields arithmetic=14 grouped=20; the second yields left=8 a=4 b=4. Since 100 AND 010 is 000, the last comparison yields bit absent=1.

sections.title: 3. Sequencing and readable repairs
paragraphs: Logical && and || sequence the left operand before any evaluated right operand. The conditional operator sequences the condition before the selected branch. Separate full expressions, such as consecutive expression statements, give a clear boundary for updates.

Parentheses cannot repair unsequenced updates. (i++) + (i++) is still undefined. Repair it with int first=i++; followed by int second=i++; and then compute first+second if the increments and sum stay in range.

For exam traces, first add grouping parentheses, then determine operand types, then identify short-circuit paths and side effects. If the execution violates a language rule, explain the violation instead of inventing a numeric answer.

revision: Explain why parentheses do not impose general execution order.
Repair a bit test with explicit grouping.

questions.question: What does 18 - 6 - 3 produce?
answer: Subtraction groups left to right: (18-6)-3 = 9. It does not group as 18-(6-3), which would produce 15.

questions.question: Why does flags & mask == 0 need parentheses?
answer: Equality binds more strongly than bitwise AND. Without parentheses the comparison happens as a grouped operand of &: flags & (mask==0). The intended expression compares the result of AND, so write (flags & mask)==0.

questions.question: Does (f()) + (g()) force f to run first?
answer: No. Those parentheses only group the call expressions. C does not impose that operand order for +. Use separate statements when one call must precede the other.
